polityNote: Regions of the Republic of Kazakhstan from independence (16 Dec 1991) to the last region-level transfer before the Natural Earth layout (10 Apr 1999; KAZ.json draws from then). Atoms: geoBoundaries KAZ ADM2 (174 districts, ODbL; stated as OpenStreetMap 2017, but the district names — Shuchinsk, Tselinny, Sovetsky, Leninogorsk, no Eskeldi — are those of about 1999–2000, and city territories are folded into districts). It is a clean partition (0 overlaps measured at 0.1°) at 22,675 vertices — finer than the Natural Earth units it replaces (6,331). A 1991 region is drawn only where every 1997 district merger on its line is shown to have stayed on one side.

sources.title: Википедия — Талды-Курганская область
sources.says: In 1989 the oblast had the Taldy-Kurgan and Tekeli city soviets and 11 districts (Aksu, Alakol, Andreyev, Burlyu-Tobe, Gvardeysky, Kapal, Karatal, Kirov, Panfilov, Sarkand, Taldy-Kurgan); abolished 1997.

sources.title: Википедия — Алматинская область
sources.says: In April 1997 the districts of the abolished Taldy-Kurgan oblast passed to Almaty oblast; in May the Gvardeysky, Kapal, Kegen, Kurty, Uygentas and Chilik districts were abolished.

sources.title: Википедия — Кербулакский район
sources.says: In 1997 the district passed to Almaty oblast and took in the abolished Gvardeysky district (both of the former Taldy-Kurgan oblast).

sources.title: Википедия — Аксуский район
sources.says: In 1967–1997 in Taldy-Kurgan oblast; in May 1997 it received the abolished Kapal district.

sources.title: Википедия — Бурлю-Тобинский район
sources.says: Abolished 28 Feb 1997, its territory divided between the Aksu, Kapal, Karatal and Sarkand districts (all of Taldy-Kurgan oblast).

sources.title: Википедия — Куртинский район
sources.says: Kurty district of Alma-Ata oblast was abolished on 23 May 1997, its rural okrugs divided between the Balkhash, Zhambyl and Ili districts.

spans.dateNote: The 1997–98 district mergers were all inside the former oblast (Gvardeysky into Kerbulak, Kapal into Aksu, Uygentas into Alakol, Burlyu-Tobe divided among Taldykorgan districts); Kurty, the Almaty-oblast district on the line, was divided among Almaty-oblast districts.

sources.title: Википедия — Кокшетауская область
sources.says: In 1989 the oblast had 15 districts and the Kokchetav and Shchuchinsk city soviets; abolished 3 May 1997.

sources.title: Википедия — Ленинградский район (Кокчетавская область)
sources.says: Abolished 2 May 1997 into the newly formed Akzhar district of Kokshetau oblast, which passed to North Kazakhstan the next day.

sources.title: Википедия — Тайыншинский район
sources.says: On 2 May 1997 Krasnoarmeysk district was renamed Tayynsha and took in the abolished Keller and Chkalov districts (all of Kokshetau oblast).

sources.title: Википедия — Айыртауский район
sources.says: On 2 May 1997 the abolished Arykbalyk district joined Ayyrtau; on 3 May the district, like all of Kokshetau oblast, passed to North Kazakhstan.

sources.title: Википедия — Район имени Габита Мусрепова
sources.says: On 2 May 1997 the district took in the abolished Ruzayevka and Chistopol districts and was renamed Tselinny; on 3 May it passed from Kokshetau to North Kazakhstan.

sources.title: Википедия — Уалихановский район
sources.says: On 2 May 1997 Kzyltu district absorbed part of the abolished Valikhanov district (both of Kokshetau oblast) and became Ualikhanov district.

sources.title: Википедия — Кокчетавский район
sources.says: Abolished 2 May 1997, its territory joined Zerendi district of Kokshetau oblast.

sources.title: Википедия — Акмолинская область
sources.says: On 22 Apr 1997 five districts of Torgay oblast passed to Akmola; on 10 Apr 1999 the Zerendi, Shchuchinsk and Enbekshilder districts with Kokshetau passed from North Kazakhstan to Akmola.

spans.dateNote: The mergers of 2 May 1997 (Akzhar, Tayynsha, Ayyrtau, Tselinny, Ualikhanov, Zerendi) were made inside Kokshetau oblast the day before it was abolished; Kokshetau city lies in the Zerendi atom.

spans.dateNote: Named Tselinograd oblast until 1992; Akmola city (Astana) was a city of the oblast and lies in the Tselinograd district atom.

sources.title: Википедия — Тургайская область (Казахстан)
sources.says: Restored 17 Aug 1990 from districts of Kustanay and Tselinograd oblasts; abolished 22 Apr 1997, its districts divided between Akmola and Kustanay oblasts.

sources.title: Википедия — Карасуский район
sources.says: In August 1997 the territory of the abolished Oktyabrsky district of former Torgay oblast was joined to Karasu district.

spans.dateNote: With the Torgay districts of Arkalyk, Amangeldy, Amantogay, Dzhangeldy and Oktyabrsky.

sources.title: Википедия — Семипалатинская область (Казахстан)
sources.says: Abolished 3 May 1997, its whole territory passed to East Kazakhstan oblast.

sources.title: Википедия — Кокпектинский район
sources.says: On 23 May 1997 the territory of the abolished Samarsky district of East Kazakhstan oblast was included in Kokpekty district (of former Semipalatinsk oblast).

sources.title: Википедия — Жезказганская область
sources.says: In 1989 the oblast had four city soviets (Balkhash, Dzhezkazgan, Karazhal, Nikolsky) and the Agadyr, Aktogay, Dzhezdy, Zhanaarka, Priozerny, Ulytau and Shet districts.

sources.title: Википедия — Карагандинская область
sources.says: In 1997 Zhezkazgan oblast with its districts and cities joined Karaganda oblast; the Agadyr, Zhezdy, Kazybekbi, Molodezhny, Telman, Tengiz and Tokyraun districts were abolished.

sources.title: Википедия — Агадырский район
sources.says: Abolished 23 May 1997, its whole territory passed to Shet district (both of former Zhezkazgan oblast).

sources.title: Википедия — Жезды (посёлок)
sources.says: Zhezdy, centre of the former Zhezdy district, lies in Ulytau district.

spans.dateNote: The 1997 abolitions inside the former oblast (Agadyr into Shet, Tokyraun into Aktogay, Zhezdy into Ulytau) stayed inside it; its cities (Balkhash, Zhezkazgan, Karazhal, Satpayev) lie inside these atoms.
